cards.hook: 22 todos shipped, a breakthrough feature landed — and the anxiety support system stayed silent for 16 days.

cards.headline: The engine is running. Check the fuel.
cards.body: You came home from the honeymoon with a plan and you executed it — 22 todos completed, the Ask Gremly chat function shipped, fitness back on track. But the same week delivered three separate anxiety episodes and the mental wellbeing habit that's supposed to catch all of that has now been untouched for 16 consecutive days.
cards.quote: Grateful to be home after an amazing trip. Feeling hopefully for getting back to some normalcy an the motivation I have for Gremly. Bring it on
cards.image_hint: San Francisco morning fog clearing over city hills

moments.title: Dave's news cracked something open
moments.body: You wrote two journal entries on the same day. The first: focused, productive, keeping pace. The second — hours later, after Dave got the Decagon job — pivoted in a single sentence: 'If the app doesn't work I don't know what I'll do as I really don't enjoy working at Dentsu anymore.' Then you caught yourself: 'But it's not about me today.' The pride was real. So was the fear it unlocked.
moments.image_hint: overcast SF skyline late afternoon fog

moments.title: The body sent the bill
moments.body: You played tennis, shipped the general chat function in half a day, and felt genuinely proud of it. Then a restaurant — too loud, a hangover, the lorazepam weaning — and the journal entry cuts off mid-sentence: 'My anxiety came when I was in a restaurant with a lot of overwhelming sounds, with hangover and anxiety so I wonder if its all because of th—' Sleep debt, sensory overwhelm, and a compounding withdrawal effect arriving all at once. You named it and kept going.
moments.image_hint: rain on window condensation evening blur

spotlight.title: The support system dropped first — not last
spotlight.takeaway: Fitness, sobriety, and Gremly all came back after the honeymoon. The mental wellbeing habit did not — and anxiety filled the gap.
spotlight.evidence_trail: App Development & Launch: 22 todos completed, highest output since TestFlight. Running: 2/3 weekly target hit. Strength Training: re-engaged March 28. Sobriety: 4/7 days logged. Mental Wellbeing: 0 completions for 16 consecutive days — while anxiety appeared on March 26 (career worry, Dave's job), March 28 (sensory overwhelm, lorazepam weaning), and March 29 (anxious mood). The habit with 11 completions across six weeks through March 13 was the first dropped and the last to return.

research_context.title: Why this happens
research_context.body: Wendy Wood's 2021 research on habit reinstatement shows that after disruption, people restore habits in order of perceived urgency and social visibility — fitness and work habits return first because their absence is externally noticeable. Internal regulation practices are invisible to others and return last, or not at all.
sources: Wood (2021) — Good Habits, Bad Habits: Reinstatement after disruption

primary.title: Restart the mental wellbeing habit — one day
primary.body: Not a streak. Not a system. One completion this week. The habit had 11 completions through March 13 and has been at zero for 16 days while anxiety appeared on three separate days. The work meeting cadence resumes Monday — that's the moment to put it back.

secondary.title: Name the lorazepam weaning to someone
secondary.body: You flagged it in a chat note on March 28 as a compounding factor for anxiety. It deserves a conversation with a doctor or therapist, not just a journal mention.

secondary.title: Let the pre-launch audit be the week's shape
secondary.body: The 12-todo triage batch on March 29 already defined the next phase. Resist adding new features this week — the audit is the work.

More importantly: you ran, lifted, and shipped a feature you called game-changing, all in the same week. The one thing that didn't come back was the thought management habit. That's the thing worth protecting this week — not as a streak, just once.
